newsitem.title: USA: Merrill sees Colombia 96/97 coffee at 9.4-10.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Merrill sees Colombia 96/97 coffee at 9.4-10.5 mln.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said Colombia's coffee output will likely come in at a "vastly reduced" 9.4 to 10.5 million 60-kg bags for the 1996/97 crop year.

"Data for the first four months of the season show production at the lowest level in nearly 20 years," softs commodities analyst Judith Ganes said in a bi-weekly commodity trends outlook. "We could see the crop range between 9.4 million bags to a high of 10.5 million bags."
By comparison, the 1995/96 crop came in at around 12.9 million bags, while yields in the early 1990s surpassed 15 million.
"The prospect of a vastly reduced Colombian crop at a time when Central American production is also falling below expectations should keep a strong upward bias to the market," the report said.
The latest Merrill assessment compares with estimates, repeated last week, by Colombian coffee officials who put the 1996/97 crop at 10.4 million bags.
While the report notes that estimates for Brazil's upcoming 1997/98 crop have hovered around 24 million bags, Ganes told Reuters that the consensus on the crop has now shifted higher.
"Now people are working with an unchanged to slightly smaller number" for Brazil, Ganes said. "The (consensus) is more in the 25 to 27 million range."
She noted that the bi-weekly Merrill Lynch outlook, dated Feb 27, was written before private coffee consultant Leon Yallouz was reported to have assessed Brazil's 1997/98 crop at 27.5 million bags.
Merrill Lynch also predicted the nearby switch on New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange could continue to widen ahead of the March contract's expiry in two weeks' time.

"Aside from the lack of actual physical coffee available in the cash market, one reason why little coffee is coming to the board despite the high premiums on the nearby months is that spot differentials are even firmer," the report said, noting that Colombian coffee was valued at a 35-cent premium to the futures price.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
